sentence_stem: Don't call Mark right now, because
correct_completion: he has just gone to bed.
full_sentence: Don't call Mark right now, because he has just gone to bed.
acceptable_variants: he has already gone to bed.

options.text: he goes to bed at ten every night.
options.why_wrong: The simple present describes a habit, not an action that has just finished, so it does not explain why the call is a bad idea right now.

options.text: he has just gone to bed.
he went to bed at ten last night.
options.why_wrong: The past simple with a finished time expression does not connect the action to the present. The present perfect with 'just' is needed here.
This is ungrammatical because the present perfect needs 'has' before the past participle 'gone'.

grammar_focus: Present perfect with 'just' to show an action completed a moment ago
explanation: The word 'just' signals an action completed a moment ago, and the present perfect links that completed action to the present situation. Ukrainian has no separate present perfect tense, so Ukrainian speakers often use a simple past form here, which is incorrect in this context.
translation: Не телефонуй Марку зараз, бо він щойно ліг спати.
